questions.q: In the Periodic Labour Force Survey, a woman spent most of the 365 days before the survey as a full-time student but worked as a paid farm labourer for 45 days in that period. In the seven days before the survey she did no work but was seeking work. How would she be classified?
o: Outside the labour force under both usual status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status
Employed under usual status (ps+ss) but unemployed under Current Weekly Status
Unemployed under usual status (ps+ss) but employed under Current Weekly Status
Employed under both usual status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status
questions.e: Her principal status over 365 days is that of a student, outside the labour force, but 45 days of paid work cross the 30-day threshold for subsidiary status, so under usual status (ps+ss) she counts as employed. Current Weekly Status looks only at the last seven days: she did no work and sought work, so she counts as unemployed. This is why CWS unemployment usually runs above the usual-status rate, which counts any substantial work over a year.

questions.q:
Match List-I (survey) with List-II (coverage):
List-I
A. Annual Survey of Industries
B. Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises
C. Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises
D. Periodic Labour Force Survey
List-II
1. Non-agricultural enterprises that are not registered as companies
2. Labour force, employment and unemployment estimates from households
3. Factories in the organised manufacturing sector
4. Service firms registered as companies or limited liability partnerships
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Annual Survey of Industries covers organised manufacturing, mainly registered factories. ASUSE covers unincorporated non-farm enterprises such as small shops, workshops and service units. ASISSE, launched in 2026 with reference year 2024-25, covers incorporated service firms under the Companies Acts or the LLP Act. The PLFS is a household survey of the labour force. All are run by the National Statistics Office of MoSPI, and the three enterprise surveys together map the non-agricultural economy.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 40; Shankar IAS pp. 51-53

questions.q:
With reference to labour-force indicators used in the Periodic Labour Force Survey, consider the following statements:
1. If the Labour Force Participation Rate stays unchanged while the Unemployment Rate falls, the Worker Population Ratio must rise.
2. The Worker Population Ratio and the Unemployment Rate can both fall in the same year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The three rates are tied by one identity: the Worker Population Ratio equals the Labour Force Participation Rate multiplied by one minus the Unemployment Rate, because unemployment is measured against the labour force, not the population. With LFPR fixed, a lower UR must mean a higher WPR. If LFPR itself falls, as when people withdraw to study or for home duties, WPR can fall even while UR falls. In 2025 an LFPR of 59.3 per cent and a WPR of 57.4 per cent went with a UR of about 3 per cent.

questions.q:
The National Statistics Office launched the Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE) in 2026. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. It covers unincorporated service enterprises such as small shops and repair units.
2. Its sampling frame is drawn from the MCA21 company registry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. ASISSE covers incorporated firms registered under the Companies Act, 1956 or 2013 or the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, in trade, transport, IT, health, education and hospitality; small unincorporated units fall under ASUSE. Its frame comes from the Goods and Services Tax Network database, which captures active service businesses, and about 1.21 lakh firms were surveyed for reference year 2024-25, the first such annual survey.

questions.q:
The PLFS was revamped from January 2025, and its first calendar-year Annual Report appeared in April 2026. With reference to the revamp, consider the following statements:
1. The survey year moved from the July-June agricultural year to the January-December calendar year.
2. Annual estimates are now published only in Current Weekly Status.
3. Quarterly Current Weekly Status estimates continue to cover only urban areas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. From January 2025 the National Statistics Office shifted the survey to the calendar year and changed the sample design. Statement 2 is wrong because annual estimates are given in both usual status and Current Weekly Status. Statement 3 is wrong because quarterly CWS estimates, once urban only, now extend to rural areas, and monthly CWS figures are produced for rural and urban India. The PLFS itself began in 2017 as the main source of labour statistics.

questions.q:
The ASUSE 2025 results were described as showing an informal sector 'trapped between survival and stagnation'. With reference to these results, consider the following statements:
1. Manufacturing accounted for the largest share of the sector's gross value added.
2. Services accounted for the largest share of establishments.
3. The survey covers agricultural enterprises along with non-farm units.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: services made up about 42 per cent of the 7.92 crore establishments, ahead of trade and manufacturing. Statement 1 is wrong because manufacturing had the smallest GVA share, about 21 per cent, behind services and trade; trade and services together produce about 80 per cent of GVA. Statement 3 is wrong as ASUSE covers only unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises. Wages rose more slowly than GVA, showing weak bargaining power.

questions.q:
Which of the following are findings of the PLFS Annual Report 2025?
1. Among women outside the labour force, the most common reason given was the wish to continue studies.
2. The share of self-employment fell while that of regular wage or salaried work rose.
3. Agriculture remained the largest employer of workers.
4. The unemployment rate was higher in urban areas than in rural areas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Self-employment fell from 57.5 to 56.2 per cent and regular salaried work rose to 23.6 per cent; agriculture's share dropped to 43 per cent but stayed the largest; urban unemployment was 4.8 per cent against 2.4 in rural areas. Statement 1 is wrong: continuing studies was the main reason for men, while 44.4 per cent of women outside the labour force cited childcare and home-making. Female LFPR stood at 40 per cent.

questions.q:
Telangana enacted the Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration, Social Security and Welfare) Act in April 2026. With reference to this Act and the Code on Social Security, 2020, consider the following statements:
1. Telangana's welfare levy on aggregators is calculated on the value of platform transactions, whereas the Code's contribution is calculated on an aggregator's annual turnover.
2. Under the Telangana Act, every aggregator, whatever the number of workers engaged, must set up an internal dispute resolution committee.
3. Under the Code, an aggregator's contribution is capped at 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers.
4. Telangana was the first State in southern India to enact such a law.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Telangana's fund draws a 1-2 per cent levy on the value of platform transactions, besides State grants and CSR money, while the Code asks aggregators for 1-2 per cent of annual turnover, capped at 5 per cent of payments to such workers. Statement 2 is wrong: the internal committee is required only of aggregators with 100 or more workers. Statement 4 is wrong: Telangana is the fifth State, after Rajasthan, Karnataka, Jharkhand and Bihar, so Karnataka came earlier in the south.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 25-27; Vision IAS pp. 34-36 for the Code's contribution

questions.q:
With reference to the four Labour Codes, consider the following pairs:
Labour Code : Provision
1. Code on Wages, 2019 : Statutory right to minimum wage for workers in both organised and unorganised sectors
2. Industrial Relations Code, 2020 : Fixed term employment
3. Industrial Relations Code, 2020 : Prior government approval for lay-off only in establishments with 300 or more workers
4. Code on Social Security, 2020 : Recognition of a union with 51 per cent membership as the negotiating union
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Code on Wages extends minimum wages to all workers, where the old Act covered only scheduled employments. The Industrial Relations Code allows fixed term employment and raised the lay-off approval threshold from 100 to 300 workers. Pair 4 is wrong: recognition of a union with 51 per cent membership as sole negotiating union is in the Industrial Relations Code. The four Codes merged 29 Central labour laws.

questions.q: Denmark's 'flexicurity' model, cited in the debate on factory-worker protests in 2026, is best described as which one of the following?
o: Guaranteed lifetime employment in large firms in return for wage restraint
A ban on contract labour in core activities of a factory
Workers elect representatives to company boards and works councils that share in management decisions
Easy hiring and firing for employers combined with generous unemployment support and active retraining for workers
questions.e: Flexicurity joins labour-market flexibility for firms with security for workers through strong unemployment benefits and active labour-market policies, so workers are protected as people rather than in a particular job. Board-level worker representation describes German co-determination, also cited as a reform idea. Lifetime employment was a feature of large Japanese firms. The model was cited as a way to deal with India's rising contract labour, about 42 per cent of manufacturing workers in 2023-24.

questions.q:
The Income Tax Act, 2025 came into force in April 2026. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. A single 'Tax Year' replaces the separate Financial Year and Assessment Year.
2. Minimum Alternate Tax applies to companies, while Alternate Minimum Tax applies to non-corporate taxpayers.
3. It revised the tax rates for individual taxpayers.
4. Virtual digital assets are included within undisclosed income for search cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Act ends the confusing FY/AY pairing, keeps MAT for 'zero-tax' companies with book profits and AMT as the parallel levy on others in separate sub-sections, and brings virtual digital assets alongside cash, bullion and jewellery in search cases; officers may also access a 'virtual digital space'. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act is a simplification that cut sections from 819 to 536 and kept tax rates, regimes and penalties unchanged.

questions.q:
Factory-worker protests in 2026 renewed debate on labour reforms. Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Industrial Relations Code, a 14-day strike notice is required only in public utility services.
2. Labour is a subject in the Concurrent List.
3. The Anoop Satpathy Committee of 2018 proposed a method for fixing a national minimum wage.
4. ILO Convention No. 144 deals with tripartite consultation among governments, employers and workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is not correct: the Code extends the 14-day notice to all industrial establishments, where the older law confined it to public utility services, which critics say makes strikes harder. The other three are correct. Because labour is in the Concurrent List, both the Centre and the States must notify rules, so implementation is uneven. The Satpathy Committee's 2018 method for a national minimum wage is still to be adopted. Convention 144 of 1976 is the basis for reviving the Indian Labour Conference, last held in 2015.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 34-36; Concurrent List entries are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Investments made before 1 April 2017 have been excluded from the General Anti-Avoidance Rules by an amendment to the Income Tax Rules, 2026.
Statement-II: The General Anti-Avoidance Rules target arrangements whose main purpose is to obtain a tax benefit.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second does not explain the first. GAAR lets the tax authority deny benefits from impermissible avoidance arrangements, which is its purpose. The exclusion in Statement-I is a matter of grandfathering: investments made before a cut-off date continue under the earlier treatment so that rules are not applied retrospectively, which gives investors certainty. The 2026 amendment removed ambiguity about that cut-off under the new Act.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 41; GAAR purpose is static

questions.q: In April 2026 the Ministry of Mines set up a Rs 5,000 crore incentive for States under the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI). Under SASCI, assistance to States takes which one of the following forms?
o: Centrally Sponsored Scheme funding shared 60:40 between the Centre and States
Grants-in-aid under Article 275(1) for capital works
Fifty-year interest-free loans for capital expenditure
Loans from NABARD's Rural Infrastructure Development Fund at concessional interest
questions.e: SASCI, run by the Finance Ministry, gives States 50-year interest-free loans for capital spending, and parts of it are tied to sectoral reforms. The mining window rewards States for implementing mining reforms, operationalising auctioned mines and reforms measured by the State Mining Readiness Index. Article 275 grants are statutory grants, NABARD's RIDF lends at interest, and a 60:40 cost-sharing pattern describes Centrally Sponsored Schemes, not this loan window.

questions.q:
Arrange the following changes to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code in chronological order:
1. A pre-packaged resolution process for MSME corporate debtors
2. A cap of 330 days for completing the corporate insolvency resolution process
3. A creditor-initiated, out-of-court insolvency resolution process
4. Temporary suspension of fresh insolvency proceedings during the pandemic
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The 330-day cap, along with the 14-day window for admission and coverage of personal guarantors, came with the 2019 amendment. The pandemic brought a temporary bar on initiating new cases through the 2020 amendment. The pre-packaged route for MSMEs arrived in 2021. The Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process is the newest, added by the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026. The Code itself dates from 2016 and set up the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.

questions.q:
The RBI released Payments Vision 2028 in April 2026. Which of the following are among its proposals or premises?
1. The banks of both the customer and the beneficiary should share liability for fraud.
2. Under the present Limiting Liability framework, liability for unauthorised frauds falls on the issuing bank alone.
3. A single-window application for authorisations under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and FEMA for cross-border payments.
4. Full interoperability across TReDS platforms, which are regulated by the RBI.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All four are correct. Payments Vision 2028 proposes joint liability of remitter and beneficiary banks, a change from the present rule that leaves unauthorised-fraud liability only with the issuer. It also proposes a single window for cross-border payment authorisations under the PSS Act, 2007 and FEMA, 1999, an on-off switch for each payment mode and oversight of e-commerce marketplaces and white-label AePS providers. TReDS, where MSMEs auction invoices to financiers, is an RBI-regulated system that would become fully interoperable.

questions.q:
Parliament passed the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. Government dues such as taxes are not to be treated as dues of a secured creditor for distribution.
2. The Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process is open to every creditor of a company.
3. Once a resolution plan is approved, earlier claims against the corporate debtor are extinguished unless the plan says otherwise.
4. The Committee of Creditors gets power to appoint and remove the liquidator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. The Act settles that statutory dues do not rank as secured claims, writes the clean-slate principle into law and gives the Committee of Creditors control over the liquidator, whose power to adjudicate claims is curtailed. Statement 2 is wrong: the new out-of-court process is available only to financial institutions notified by the Centre, which critics say favours some creditors. The Act also sets timelines such as 180 days for liquidation.

questions.q: The new Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 follows a 'debtor-in-possession' style. This means that during resolution
o: the debtor may not be admitted to insolvency unless it consents
the debtor's existing management continues to run the business while creditors pursue resolution
the debtor's assets are sold at once and the proceeds held by the court
an interim resolution professional replaces the board from the first day
questions.e: In a debtor-in-possession model the business keeps running under its own management while the process goes on, which preserves value and avoids the disruption of handing control to an outsider. The standard corporate process under the Code is creditor-in-control: a resolution professional displaces the board. Immediate sale describes liquidation, not resolution, and consent of the debtor is not the trigger, which remains a default. Critics note that value has often eroded by the time of default.

questions.q:
UPI completed ten years in April 2026. With reference to UPI, consider the following statements:
1. It is operated directly by the Reserve Bank of India.
2. UPI 123PAY is meant for smartphone users who lack internet access.
3. UPI Lite is designed for low-value payments.
4. A UPI ID removes the need to share a bank account number and IFSC for a payment.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. UPI Lite handles small payments with fewer steps, and the virtual payment address stands in for account number and IFSC. Statement 1 is wrong: UPI is run by NPCI, under RBI oversight, on the IMPS rails. Statement 2 is wrong: UPI 123PAY serves feature-phone users through options such as IVR and missed calls. UPI is the payments layer of India Stack, with over 700 banks live.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 27-30; Shankar IAS pp. 53-56

questions.q: In the context of the SEZ reforms of the Union Budget 2026-27, the 'Domestic Tariff Area' refers to which one of the following?
o: Only those parts of India that lie outside Export Oriented Units
The whole of India, including its territorial waters and continental shelf, but excluding Special Economic Zones
Areas within a fixed distance of notified customs ports
Areas where goods attract the Goods and Services Tax but not customs duty
questions.e: Under the SEZ Act, 2005 the Domestic Tariff Area is all of India, territorial waters and continental shelf included, except the SEZs, which for authorised operations are treated as outside the customs territory. This is why sales from an SEZ into the DTA count as imports under Section 30 and attract duty. The Budget allowed eligible SEZ manufacturers a one-time window to sell a capped share of output in the DTA at concessional duty, to use idle capacity hit by global trade disruption.

questions.q:
With reference to UPI's newer features, consider the following pairs:
Product : Function
1. UPI Circle : Delegated payments by a trusted user such as a minor or senior citizen, within limits
2. Credit Line on UPI : Cross-border remittances through UPI
3. Hello UPI : Voice-based payments
4. UPI Lite X : On-device wallet for payments
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct. UPI Circle lets a primary user allow another person to pay within set controls; Hello UPI uses voice commands; UPI Lite X is a device-based wallet that also works offline. Pair 2 is wrong: Credit Line on UPI links pre-sanctioned bank credit to UPI, a route to micro-credit, though its revenue remains small. Cross-border UPI works through NIPL tie-ups in countries such as the UAE, Singapore, France and Nepal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The concentration of UPI transactions in a few apps is seen as a risk to India's payments system.
Statement-II: Two apps together handle close to four-fifths of UPI transactions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. PhonePe has about 45 per cent and Google Pay about 33 per cent of UPI volumes, so an outage, policy change or exit at either could disrupt a large share of retail payments, making them close to 'too big to fail'. Members of Parliament have also noted that both leaders are foreign-owned. Paytm holds about 6 per cent, and smaller apps such as BHIM, Navi and super.money are seen as ways to widen competition.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 53-56; Vision IAS pp. 27-30

questions.q: The RBI's 2026 discussion paper on digital payment frauds focused on 'authorised push-payment' fraud. Such fraud is best described as one in which
o: a fraudster uses stolen card details to make payments without the holder's knowledge
the victim is deceived into approving a payment himself, for instance by a fake call-centre or deepfake impersonation
a bank wrongly debits a customer through a technical error in the payment system
a merchant charges a customer twice for the same purchase
questions.e: In authorised push-payment fraud the victim personally authorises the transfer after being tricked, so ordinary authentication such as a PIN does not stop it. That is why the RBI floated a one-hour delay on transfers above Rs 10,000 that the payer can cancel, approval by a trusted person for high-value payments by senior citizens, and extra checks on large credits to suspected mule accounts. Unauthorised use of stolen card data is a different category covered by the liability framework.

questions.q:
The RBI cancelled the licence of Paytm Payments Bank in April 2026. With reference to payments banks, consider the following statements:
1. They can issue credit cards to their customers.
2. They were recommended by the Nachiket Mor Committee.
3. They must invest at least 75 per cent of their demand deposits in government securities eligible for SLR.
4. They are registered under the Companies Act, 2013 and governed by the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. The Nachiket Mor Committee of 2014 proposed differentiated licences, of which payments banks and small finance banks are the two kinds. Payments banks take deposits and offer remittances but must park most funds in SLR securities and the rest with banks; they are companies governed by banking law. Statement 1 is wrong: they cannot lend, so they cannot issue credit cards, though debit cards are allowed. Paytm's licence was cancelled for breaching the licensing guidelines.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs, relating to the RBI's measures against digital payment fraud:
Measure : Description
1. MuleHunter.AI : Tool built by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub to detect mule accounts
2. Digital Payment Intelligence Platform : AI and machine-learning prototype to reduce payment-fraud risk
3. Proposed time lag in the 2026 discussion paper : One-hour delay, cancellable by the payer, for transfers above Rs 10,000
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. MuleHunter.AI, developed by the RBI's innovation subsidiary, flags accounts used to receive and move fraud proceeds. The Digital Payment Intelligence Platform is a prototype to share intelligence and score risk across the system. The one-hour cooling period with a whitelisting facility for trusted payees is the centrepiece of the 2026 paper, prompted by cyber-fraud cases rising to about 28 lakh in 2025. Two-factor authentication and tokenisation already apply.

questions.q:
In April 2026 the RBI acted on several market instruments. Consider the following pairs:
Instrument : Feature
1. Rupee Non-Deliverable Derivative : Traded offshore and settled in another currency, usually the US dollar
2. Additional Tier-1 bond : Perpetual and able to absorb losses or convert to equity
3. Net Open Position : Difference between a bank's foreign-currency assets and liabilities
4. Credit Default Swap : Protection to the buyer against default by a reference borrower
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. NDDs fix a future rupee rate but settle in dollars abroad, beyond the RBI's reach, which is why banks were barred from them. AT-1 bonds have no maturity and can be written down or converted in distress, so their mis-selling to retail investors drew action. The RBI capped banks' rupee Net Open Position at 100 million dollars. A CDS works like insurance on a bond: the buyer pays premiums and the seller pays on default.

questions.q: IRDAI introduced a financial-reporting framework for insurers based on Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) in 2026. Ind AS are notified by which one of the following?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
questions.e: Ind AS, the Indian standards converged with International Financial Reporting Standards, are notified by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The ICAI drafts them through its Accounting Standards Board, which is why it is a common wrong answer, and SEBI enforces disclosure by listed firms but does not notify accounting standards. IRDAI's move covers life, general and standalone health insurers and reinsurers, aiming at transparency and global comparability.

questions.q:
The Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 was notified in April 2026. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. It invests directly in the equity of startups.
2. SIDBI is an implementing agency.
3. Alternative Investment Funds that receive its money are selected by SEBI.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: SIDBI, which also ran the 2016 Fund of Funds, is an implementing agency along with another domestic agency to be chosen. Statement 1 is wrong because the fund contributes to SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds, which then invest in startups. Statement 3 is wrong because the AIFs are chosen by a Venture Capital Investment Committee of ecosystem veterans, under an Empowered Committee chaired by the Secretary, DPIIT. Segments include deep-tech and Micro VCs.

questions.q:
The Union Budget 2026-27 announced measures for Special Economic Zones. With reference to the SEZ framework, consider the following statements:
1. Supplies from the Domestic Tariff Area to an SEZ are treated as exports.
2. Clearances from an SEZ into the Domestic Tariff Area are treated as exports.
3. Supplies to SEZ units are zero-rated under the IGST Act, 2017.
4. Free Trade Warehousing Zones can be set up within the SEZ framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Section 2(m) of the SEZ Act, 2005 treats supplies into an SEZ as exports, and the IGST Act zero-rates them; units may also provide warehousing through Free Trade Warehousing Zones. Statement 2 is wrong: Section 30 treats goods moving from an SEZ into the domestic market as imports that attract full duty. That is why the Budget's one-time concessional-duty window for SEZ manufacturers selling in the domestic market matters to units with idle capacity.

questions.q: The national agriculture market e-NAM, which by 2026 linked 1,656 mandis, is implemented by which one of the following as its lead agency?
o: National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India (NAFED)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.e: e-NAM, an online trading platform that links regulated mandis so that farmers can sell to buyers beyond their local market, was launched in 2016 and is run by the Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium under the Agriculture Ministry. NAFED handles procurement such as oilseeds under PM-AASHA, NABARD refinances rural credit, and the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection deals with grading and market regulation. e-NAM now covers 23 States and 4 UTs, with FPOs among its traders.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 61-64; SFAC as lead agency is static

questions.q:
With reference to India's export zones, consider the following pairs:
Place : Feature
1. Kandla : Asia's first Export Processing Zone
2. GIFT City : Port-led SEZ handling bulk cargo
3. Sanand : Among the first SEZs for semiconductors under the 2025 rule change
4. Dharwad : Among the first SEZs for electronic components under the 2025 rule change
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Kandla's EPZ of 1965 was a pioneer, but controls and weak infrastructure hampered the EPZ model until the SEZ policy of 2000 and the SEZ Act, 2005. The June 2025 amendment allowed SEZs exclusively for semiconductors and electronic components, with relaxed land and encumbrance norms; Sanand and Dharwad were the first. Pair 2 is wrong: GIFT City is a financial-services hub, whereas Mundra and Kandla are the port-led examples.

questions.q:
With reference to issues at the WTO's Fourteenth Ministerial Conference at Yaounde in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The SPS Agreement deals with measures for human, animal and plant health.
2. The TBT Agreement deals with sanitary measures on imported food.
3. MC14 adopted comprehensive disciplines on fisheries subsidies.
4. The Ministerial Conference meets every year.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Sanitary and phytosanitary measures cover food safety and animal and plant health, while the TBT Agreement covers technical regulations, standards and conformity assessment, so statement 2 confuses the two; MC14 sought stronger special and differential treatment under both. Statement 3 is wrong: members only agreed to continue negotiations towards comprehensive fisheries disciplines by MC15. Statement 4 is wrong: the Ministerial Conference, the WTO's top body, meets every two years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The US announcement of a 100 per cent duty on patented pharmaceuticals in April 2026 was expected to have limited impact on India.
Statement-II: Generic drugs, which dominate India's pharma exports to the US, were excluded from the duty for the time being.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. The US takes almost 40 per cent of India's pharma exports, but these are mostly generics, which were left out 'at this time'. The duty is ad valorem, a percentage of the declared value, unlike a specific duty charged per unit of weight or quantity, so it rises with the value of the drug. The risk remains that the exclusion could be withdrawn later.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 44; ad valorem concept is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India opposed adding the Investment Facilitation for Development agreement to the WTO rulebook at MC14.
Statement-II: Bringing a plurilateral text into Annex 4 could bypass the WTO's practice of decision by consensus among all members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second gives India's reason. The IFD agreement, backed by a large group of members, aims to ease FDI procedures on an MFN basis. India argues that investment lies outside the WTO's trade mandate and that slotting a text agreed by a subset into Annex 4 would let groups of members make rules without consensus. India also opposed extending the moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, citing revenue loss.

questions.q:
With reference to schemes announced or extended in April 2026, consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Associated with
1. Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
2. Vishwa Sutra : Powerlooms, with the Textiles Committee
3. Technology Development and Investment Promotion scheme : Telecom technologies including 5G Advanced and 6G
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 3 is correct: the revised TDIP for 2026-31 supports 5G Advanced and 6G work by startups, MSMEs, academia and operators through TSDSI, TCoE India and TCIL. Pair 1 is wrong because RoSCTL is a Ministry of Textiles scheme of 2019 that rebates embedded taxes on apparel and made-ups through duty credit scrips. Pair 2 is wrong because Vishwa Sutra, 'Weaves of India for the World', is about handlooms and was initiated by the Development Commissioner (Handlooms) with NIFT.

questions.q:
With reference to global economic reports, some of which assessed India's prospects in April 2026, consider the following pairs:
Publication : Brought out by
1. Economic and Social Survey of Asia and the Pacific : Asian Development Bank
2. World Economic Outlook : International Monetary Fund
3. Global Economic Prospects : World Bank
4. Fiscal Monitor : International Monetary Fund
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are correct. The IMF's World Economic Outlook, issued twice a year, raised India's FY27 forecast to 6.5 per cent in April 2026 and ranked India sixth by nominal GDP; the Fiscal Monitor and the Global Financial Stability Report are its other flagships. The Global Economic Prospects is the World Bank's flagship. Pair 1 is wrong: the Economic and Social Survey of Asia and the Pacific comes from UN ESCAP, which projected India at 6.4 per cent; the ADB publishes the Asian Development Outlook.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 48-51; Global Economic Prospects and Asian Development Outlook are static

questions.q:
The FAO Food Price Index rose in March 2026 on higher energy costs. Which of the following commodity groups make up this index?
1. Cereals
2. Vegetable oils
3. Fish and seafood
4. Sugar
5. Dairy
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The index tracks monthly changes in international prices of five groups: cereals, vegetable oils, dairy, meat and sugar, against a 2014-16 base. Fish is not one of them, which makes the choice that includes it wrong, and any choice leaving out sugar or dairy is incomplete. The March 2026 reading of 128.5 points reflected higher energy costs during the West Asia conflict, which feed into fertiliser, transport and processing costs.

questions.q:
With reference to the UN Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), consider the following statements:
1. Its headquarters is in Bangkok.
2. Its membership is limited to countries located in Asia and the Pacific.
3. It reports directly to the UN General Assembly.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. ESCAP began in 1947 as the Economic Commission for Asia and the Far East, with India as a founding member, and is based in Bangkok. Statement 2 is wrong: its 53 members include non-regional States such as the United Kingdom and France, besides nine associate members. Statement 3 is wrong: it is one of five UN regional commissions, all of which report to the Economic and Social Council.

questions.q:
Developing countries launched a 'Borrowers' Platform' at the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings in 2026. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. It is a forum that restructures the debts of its members by negotiating with creditors.
2. Its secretariat is provided by the International Monetary Fund.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. The platform is explicitly not a debt-restructuring forum; it offers peer learning, capacity building in debt management and a stronger collective voice for borrowers in sovereign-debt talks long led by creditor groups such as the Paris Club. Its secretariat is UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), not the IMF, and Egypt chairs its 30 founding members, who include India. Borrowers' external debt reached about 11.7 trillion dollars in 2024.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Electrical conductivity
2. Organic carbon
3. Boron
4. Soil moisture
How many of the above are among the parameters reported on a Soil Health Card?
questions.e: Electrical conductivity, organic carbon and boron are among the twelve parameters: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron, pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon. Soil moisture is not reported, since it changes from day to day and the card is meant to guide nutrient use over seasons. About 25.55 crore cards had been issued by November 2025, and the card supports balanced fertiliser use, a weakness flagged in the 2026 review of Indian agriculture.

questions.q:
India recorded foodgrain output of 357.73 million tonnes in 2024-25. With reference to India's position in world production as reported, consider the following pairs:
Commodity : India's rank
1. Pulses : First
2. Millets : First
3. Coffee : Second
4. Dry onions : First
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. India is the largest producer of pulses, millets and dry onions, the last accounting for about a quarter of world output, as well as spices and coconut. Pair 3 is wrong: India ranks only about seventh in coffee, grown mainly in Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, though it is second in tea, wheat, sugarcane, fruits and vegetables. Rice is left out here because the two magazines differ on its rank.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 22-23; Shankar IAS pp. 61-64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Foreign portfolio investors remained net sellers of Indian equities through 2025-26 even as domestic institutional inflows stayed strong.
Statement-II: Indian equities traded at a large valuation premium to other emerging markets while earnings growth looked capped.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. Paying about 20 times earnings for 10-15 per cent growth, a premium of roughly half over emerging-market peers, looked unattractive when China, Taiwan, South Korea and Brazil offered themes such as AI, semiconductors and governance reform. Domestic investors absorbed the selling, so markets did not crash, but foreign ownership fell to a 15-year low. Analysts debate whether the causes are cyclical rotation or structural weaknesses.

questions.q:
With reference to Minimum Support Prices (MSP) in India, consider the following statements:
1. The mandated crops include jute and copra.
2. Sugarcane is among the 22 mandated crops for which MSP is announced.
3. Since 2018-19, MSPs have been fixed at a level of at least one and a half times the all-India weighted average cost of production.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The 22 mandated crops are 14 kharif crops, six rabi crops and two commercial crops, jute and copra, and since 2018-19 MSPs have been set at least 1.5 times the cost of production. Statement 2 is wrong: sugarcane is priced separately through a Fair and Remunerative Price fixed under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, though the CACP advises on it too. MSP is an administrative price, not a legal entitlement, which is why farm groups seek a statutory guarantee.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 61-64; crop list and FRP are static

questions.q:
With reference to schemes for agriculture, which of the statements given below is/are NOT correct?
1. PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme.
2. PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana provides a pension for small and marginal farmers.
3. The Sub-Mission on Seeds and Planting Materials is part of the Green Revolution-Krishonnati Yojana.
4. The National Food Security and Nutrition Mission is a Central Sector scheme.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Only statement 4 is incorrect: the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission, covering rice, wheat, pulses and coarse cereals, is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with cost-sharing by States. PM-KISAN is fully funded by the Centre and had paid over Rs 4.27 lakh crore in 22 instalments by March 2026. Maandhan is a contributory pension for small and marginal farmers. The seeds sub-mission, under Krishonnati, supports seed villages and quality seed.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 61-64; Vision IAS pp. 22-23

questions.q: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL), which is exploring lithium blocks in Argentina, is a joint venture of which of the following?
o: ONGC Videsh, Coal India Ltd and NMDC
NMDC, Coal India Ltd and Indian Rare Earths Ltd
NALCO, NMDC and Hindustan Zinc Ltd
NALCO, Hindustan Copper Ltd and Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Ltd
questions.e: KABIL was formed in 2019 by three public sector firms under the Ministry of Mines: National Aluminium Company, Hindustan Copper and Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Ltd. Its task is to identify, acquire and develop strategic minerals such as lithium and cobalt abroad for supply to India. The other combinations mix in firms from steel, coal, rare earths or oil, none of which are partners. Argentina belongs to the Lithium Triangle with Bolivia and Chile.

questions.q:
A Parliamentary Standing Committee report on oilseeds and pulses was in the news in 2026. With reference to edible oils, consider the following statements:
1. Palm oil makes up the largest share of India's edible-oil imports.
2. Most of India's oilseed area is irrigated.
3. Under PM-AASHA, oilseeds are procured at MSP through central nodal agencies such as NAFED.
4. The Committee recommended removing all customs duty on crude palm oil.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Palm oil is about 60 per cent of imports, which meet roughly 56 per cent of demand, and the Price Support Scheme under PM-AASHA procures oilseeds at MSP through NAFED and similar agencies. Statement 2 is wrong: over 70 per cent of oilseeds are rainfed, exposing them to weather. Statement 4 is wrong: the Committee wanted dynamic duties, including a 20 per cent safeguard duty on palm oil if world prices fall below 800 dollars a tonne, to protect growers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Disruption in the Gulf raises the cost of urea in India even though India produces most of the urea it uses.
Statement-II: Urea is made from ammonia that is produced mainly from natural gas, much of which India imports.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. Ammonia, the base of urea, is made from natural gas, so higher LNG prices and supply cuts raise domestic production costs; India also imports urea, about 63 per cent of it from the Gulf. Shutdowns such as at Qatar Fertiliser Company pushed urea prices up 30-40 per cent. Costlier fertiliser can cut use, lower yields and raise food prices, while swelling the subsidy bill.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 59-61; urea chemistry is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A low seed replacement rate is one of the reasons for low oilseed yields in India.
Statement-II: The seed replacement rate measures the share of area sown with certified or quality seed rather than farm-saved seed.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. Farm-saved seed loses vigour and purity over successive seasons, so a low rate of replacement with quality seed keeps yields low. The Committee found rates from 25 per cent in groundnut to 62 per cent in rapeseed-mustard against a target of 80-85 per cent, and wanted a National Commission to cap seed prices, a new Seeds Bill and the SATHI portal for seed traceability. It also backed gene editing for better varieties.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 36-38; SRR definition is static

questions.q:
With reference to India's fertiliser position amid the West Asia conflict of 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India is the world's largest consumer of fertilisers.
2. India meets most of its potash needs from domestic mines.
3. The Gulf supplies most of India's imports of Di-ammonium Phosphate.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. India is the second-largest consumer of fertilisers, after China, and the third-largest producer, so statement 1 fails. Statement 2 is wrong: India has no commercial potash output and imports almost all its Muriate of Potash. Statement 3 is wrong: about 32 per cent of DAP imports come from the Gulf; it is urea where the Gulf supplies most, about 63 per cent. Domestic DAP output meets only about 40 per cent of demand.

questions.q:
Consider the following sectors:
1. Drones and drone components
2. Shipbuilding
3. Leather footwear
4. Toys
How many of the above are among the 14 sectors covered by the Production Linked Incentive scheme?
questions.e: Only drones are among the 14 sectors, which also include mobiles and components, IT hardware, telecom, white goods, textiles (man-made fibre and technical), food products, speciality steel, ACC batteries, APIs, automobiles, solar PV modules, pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Shipbuilding, leather footwear and toys are not covered. A Parliamentary Standing Committee has asked for extending PLI to labour-intensive sectors such as leather, apparel, chemicals and handicrafts, because the existing sectors are capital-intensive and create few jobs.

questions.q:
With reference to recent railway projects, consider the following pairs:
Item : Description
1. Pamban Bridge : India's first vertical-lift sea bridge
2. Bairabi-Sairang line : Connects Aizawl to the national rail network
3. Amrit Bharat Station Scheme : Redevelopment of stations, especially in tier-2 and tier-3 cities
4. Vande Bharat Express : Indigenous semi-high-speed train introduced in 2019
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. The Pamban bridge carries the line to Rameswaram island with a span that lifts vertically for ships. The Bairabi-Sairang line brought Mizoram's capital onto the network, and work continues towards Imphal and Kohima. The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme of 2022 covers more than 1,300 stations. Vande Bharat trains run at up to 160 km per hour, with sleeper versions planned. Kavach is the separate indigenous train-protection system for safety.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Incentives under the Production Linked Incentive scheme are linked to incremental sales over a base year.
Statement-II: Job creation under the scheme has been modest because many supported plants are capital-intensive and automated.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct but unrelated as cause and effect. Linking incentives to incremental sales, the design since 2020, rewards scale and output growth; it does not explain why jobs are few. Low job creation stems from the choice of sectors such as electronics, solar PV and ACC batteries, where plants are capital-intensive. The PLI for food processing drew over Rs 9,000 crore of investment, above the Rs 7,000 crore committed, and India turned into a net exporter of mobile phones.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 30-32; Shankar IAS p. 64

questions.q:
Construction of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor was completed in 2026. With reference to Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) in India, consider the following statements:
1. The proposed East Coast corridor would link Kharagpur with Vijayawada.
2. The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd is a special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways.
3. The corridors are designed for diesel traction to haul heavy freight.
4. Freight trains on the corridors can run at speeds of up to 100 km/h.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. New corridors under examination include East Coast (Kharagpur-Vijayawada), East-West and a North-South sub-corridor. DFCCIL, set up in 2006 as a Railways SPV, plans, finances, builds and runs the corridors, where freight trains can reach 100 km/h, far faster than on crowded mixed lines. Statement 3 is wrong: the corridors are fully electrified, which helps shift freight from road to rail and cut emissions. The western corridor runs about 1,506 km from Dadri to JNPT.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 45; Shankar IAS p. 66; construction completion checked outside the notes (trial run on the last section, March 2026)

questions.q:
In In Re: Phalodi Accident, the Supreme Court issued nationwide directions on highway safety in 2026. With reference to this, consider the following statements:
1. The Court held that a safe commuting environment is part of the right to life under Article 21.
2. The Court used Article 142 to make its directions enforceable across the country.
3. SDG target 3.6 aims to halve global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Court read the commuter's right to safety into Article 21 and said financial or administrative limits cannot outweigh life. Using Article 142, it ordered a stop to new structures in the right of way, traffic management systems on all national highways, district highway safety task forces and ambulances at set intervals. National highways are about 2 per cent of road length but about 30 per cent of deaths, which is why SDG 3.6 is cited.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 38-40; SDG 3.6 is static

questions.q: Under the operational guidelines issued by MoHUA in 2026, how is a project under the Urban Challenge Fund to be financed?
o: At least half from the Fund, with the rest shared by the State and the urban local body
Twenty-five per cent from the Fund, at least fifty per cent from market sources, and the rest from States, urban local bodies or the market
Sixty per cent from the Centre and forty per cent from the State
Entirely from the Fund for cities above ten lakh population, and half from the Fund for smaller cities
questions.e: The Fund pays a quarter of project cost, at least half must be raised from markets through bonds, bank loans or private partners, and the remaining quarter comes from States, cities or further market finance. The design aims to turn Rs 1 lakh crore into about Rs 4 lakh crore of investment, with competitive selection and reform-linked release. Smaller cities borrowing for the first time can use the Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme, and projects already funded under AMRUT 2.0 or SBM 2.0 are excluded.

questions.q:
The Union Cabinet extended PMGSY-III to March 2028. With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in December 2000.
2. It aims at all-weather connectivity for unconnected habitations with a population of 500 or more in plains and 250 or more in special category areas.
3. Its third phase upgrades through routes and major rural links to agricultural markets, schools and hospitals.
4. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. PMGSY began on 25 December 2000 to give all-weather roads to eligible habitations, with a lower threshold for north-eastern and Himalayan States, deserts and select backward districts. Phase II upgraded 50,000 km, a component of 2016 covered left-wing extremism districts, and Phase III, from 2019, upgrades 1,25,000 km of through routes and links to markets, schools and hospitals. Phase IV, from 2024-25, connects about 25,000 more habitations. Costs are shared with States.

questions.q:
KABIL secured environmental clearance for exploring lithium blocks in Argentina in 2026. With reference to lithium, consider the following statements:
1. It is an alkaline earth metal.
2. It has the lowest density of all metals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Lithium is an alkali metal of Group 1, not an alkaline earth metal of Group 2, so statement 1 is wrong. It is the lightest of all metals, light enough to float on water, which is why it suits batteries where energy per kilogram matters. KABIL, formed in 2019 by NALCO, Hindustan Copper and MECL under the Mines Ministry, acquires strategic mineral assets abroad, such as the five Argentine blocks it is exploring.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 51; periodic group is static

questions.q:
The push for piped natural gas in 2026 drew attention to different gas fuels. Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. LPG
B. LNG
C. CNG
D. PNG
List-II
1. Natural gas cooled below about minus 160 degrees Celsius for shipping
2. Propane-butane mixture, heavier than air, supplied in cylinders
3. Natural gas stored at 200-250 kg/cm2, used mainly in vehicles
4. Natural gas supplied to homes through a pipeline network
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: LPG, a propane-butane mix from refining and gas processing, is heavier than air and comes in cylinders; about 60 per cent of it is imported, mostly from West Asia. LNG is natural gas chilled below minus 160 degrees Celsius so that it can be shipped and then regasified at terminals. CNG is natural gas compressed for use mainly as a transport fuel. PNG is natural gas piped to homes; being lighter than air it disperses if leaked, one reason it is pushed as safer.

questions.q:
The World Inequality Lab released a report on land inequality in India in 2026. With reference to its findings, consider the following statements:
1. Kerala showed the highest land inequality among the States studied.
2. Punjab had the highest share of landless rural households.
3. Villages closer to towns, highways and markets showed lower land inequality.
4. Areas once under British zamindari tenure showed higher inequality than former princely states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Kerala's land Gini was about 90 and 73 per cent of Punjab's rural households were landless; colonial zamindari areas and villages with large SC populations showed more inequality, a legacy of history. Statement 3 is wrong: closeness to towns, roads, banks and mandis went with higher inequality, as market integration changes farm and non-farm returns and pushes smallholders to sell. Nationally the top 10 per cent hold 44 per cent of land.

questions.q:
Persistent selling by foreign portfolio investors was in the news in 2026. With reference to foreign investment in India, consider the following statements:
1. Portfolio investment is made without seeking ownership control or management of the firm.
2. An investment by a foreign investor of 10 per cent or more of the paid-up equity of a listed Indian company is treated as foreign direct investment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Portfolio investors buy shares, bonds or fund units for returns and can exit quickly, unlike direct investors who seek a lasting interest and control. Indian rules draw the line at 10 per cent: a holding below it in a listed company counts as portfolio investment, and once it reaches 10 per cent it is reclassified as FDI. Since October 2024 FPIs have sold over 45 billion dollars, driven by high valuations and rival markets in North Asia.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 48-51; 10 per cent threshold is static
